title: Compact sufficient cabinet chart: redundancy-reduced revision of A1
coverage_gap: The same exact N20 LL/HH support leaves C combinations and extreme E cabinet yaws unobserved during training. Development now shows A1 at 1.00 C and 1.00 E, versus A2 at 1.00/0.90 and A3 at 1.00/0.60. A1 is already at the observed score ceiling, so the revision tests whether its cabinet-frame bias can retain transfer with less representational redundancy, fewer complete-system parameters and potentially lower fixed-method latency. It does not invent a failure mechanism to explain aggregate truncations.
reusable_regularity: World hand position plus cabinet-relative hand-handle error, goal-handle error, hand/handle displacements and cabinet yaw suffice to reconstruct all current/previous positions. Explicit redundant copies of those positions/errors and the aperture difference need not be supplied separately. A sign-canonical unit quaternion can also be expressed by three modified Rodrigues parameters without dropping tilt information. Keep the successful parent's static cabinet action frame and physical feature scales while reducing condition_dim from 44 to 25.
dependencies_preserved: Let R=Rz(cabinet_yaw), u=hand-handle in cabinet coordinates and v=goal-handle in cabinet coordinates after undoing feature scales. Then handle_world=hand_world-R*u and goal_world=handle_world+R*v. Keeping world hand and yaw therefore preserves absolute robot/world/goal geometry even though direct world-handle/world-goal copies are removed.

From cabinet hand/handle displacement vectors dh,do: previous_hand=hand-R*dh and previous_handle=handle-R*do. Previous relative errors in A1 are recoverable by linear arithmetic. Both current and previous apertures remain explicit and determine aperture change.

Each current/previous xyzw object quaternion is normalized, left-multiplied by inverse cabinet yaw, and assigned a deterministic w>=0 hemisphere. Store p=q_xyz/(1+q_w). The inverse is q_xyz=2p/(1+dot(p,p)), q_w=(1-dot(p,p))/(1+dot(p,p)); multiply by cabinet yaw to recover world orientation. Thus the full physical orientation is preserved up to quaternion double cover, not reduced to a guessed hinge angle. Exactly w=0 uses a deterministic vector-component sign convention.

World hand position and cabinet sine/cosine remain direct features, retaining workspace, table/world and fixed-finger alignment dependence. Physical panel orientation and relative geometry preserve the supplied door/cabinet obstacle dependencies. Only declared absent object2 zeros are omitted.

Native actions retain exactly A1's mapping: xyz encode=Rz(yaw_start)^T native_xyz, decode=Rz(yaw_start) encoded_xyz. This is one fixed chunk-start frame for every one of the sixteen predictions. No scaling, action offset, clipping, learned controller, gripper transformation, future frame or executor modification. Host still clips native world action4 and executes four actions.

evidence_refs.detail: A1 C=20/20 and E=20/20, all C/E cells at 1.0; A2 E LL=3/5 with two native_truncated episodes; A3 E HH=0/5 and LH=2/5 with eight native_truncated episodes. A1/A2/A3 frozen-rule scores are 1.00/0.95/0.80. These bundled changes do not isolate a causal effect of action frame, graph or auxiliary loss.

Measured fixed-method latencies: A1 0.1375758955036872 s, A2 0.12381885749346111 s, A3 0.1228789985034382 s. A1 has 4,732,484 parameters and the fewest parameters among those three but is not the fastest measured. Reducing A4 dimensions is only a latency hypothesis; the frozen measured latency tie-break, not a parameter proxy, will govern selection.
Selected A1 as the unique C/E-score maximizer; neither IID nor training loss nor faster losing candidates were used to override the score rule.
Same door__N20__rep0 twenty demonstrations, no additional support or development-state reads.
Static cabinet yaw, world hand/handle/goal positions, full current/previous xyzw orientation, fixed native gripper orientation and action cube require preserving frame and world dependencies.
Robot and fixed table/world context must not be discarded while canonicalizing layout.
Dynamic panel rotation motivates retaining full current/previous orientation despite compacting its representation.
Previously inspected obs 0-2, 35-40 and 60-64 distinguish approach/descent from handle motion; h-handle, goal-handle and displacement features remain direct.
Previously inspected obs 113-114 retain small contact offset late in opening; the direct hand-handle vector is not compressed away.
One common U-Net, condition per whole observation, causal action frames, unchanged optimizer and mask-normalized action epsilon loss.

expected_failure_signature: Information preservation does not imply equal learnability. If redundant A1 features supplied useful shortcuts, A4 can have poorer acquisition or late-pull precision despite retaining enough information to reconstruct them. Any loss of C/E success disproves the useful-compression hypothesis for this slot.

The hemisphere orientation chart has a discontinuity at a relative rotation of pi. A rollout approaching that boundary can exhibit abrupt conditioning changes even though the physical orientation changes smoothly. Unlike a planar-angle simplification it retains tilt, but is less globally smooth than A1's rotation columns.

With no A1 development failures, no success improvement can be inferred in advance. Matching the observed ceiling on these finite episodes is not evidence of perfect population success. Fewer condition coordinates also may not lower measured latency because U-Net convolutions dominate.
If A4 ties A1 on the fixed C/E score but is slower, it will not be chosen merely because it has fewer parameters. No checkpoint search, new seeds or extra training will be used to repair this result.
support_fit: None. Retain A1's fixed 0.1 m contact, 0.5 m scene and 0.01 m displacement scales. No other-dataset statistics, chart fit, pretraining, auxiliary loss, trainable feature encoder or weights transferred from the parent.
architecture: Condition features: contact3 + goal-error3 + hand-displacement3 + handle-displacement3 + aperture2 + full-orientation-chart current3/previous3 + world-hand3 + cabinet-yaw2 =25 per observation. Exactly one factory action4 U-Net, no additional modules, common action epsilon weight1 and denominator mask.sum()*4. The host performs a fresh fixed 20,000-update training slot and final EMA evaluation.

change_summary.change: Based on the completed A1-A3 feedback and q3=A1. Remove A1's redundant previous relative-position vectors, explicit world handle/goal copies and aperture-difference feature; replace each six-column orientation encoding by a three-coordinate full-orientation chart. Change condition44 to condition25, preserving A1's static cabinet action map and all physical observation dependencies. This is one new scientific training slot, not an edit or checkpoint selection for A1. A2/A3 negative E results remain recorded; their extra mechanisms are not inherited.
